subject: Animation
title: Kubo and the Two Strings: Pushing Boundaries
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Kubo and the Two Strings: Pushing Boundaries.

hook.text: Laika built a sixteen-foot skeleton puppet for Kubo and the Two Strings — the largest ever in stop-motion.

buildup.text: The film blended Japanese mythology with breathtaking visual ambition that stunned audiences and critics.

discovery.text: Laika combined stop-motion, CGI, and practical effects so seamlessly that viewers could not tell which was which.

twist.text: Kubo earned just $77 million against a $60 million budget. Critical acclaim did not translate to profit.

climax.text: Kubo is considered Laika's artistic peak, even if the audience never fully showed up for it.

punchline.text: Stop-motion's most ambitious film deserved a bigger audience.

quiz.question: What technical achievement did Kubo and the Two Strings accomplish?
options: It was the first stop-motion film in color
It built the largest stop-motion puppet ever and seamlessly blended stop-motion with CGI
It was animated entirely by one person

details.summary: Kubo and the Two Strings (2016) pushed stop-motion to epic scale with a 16-foot skeleton puppet and seamless CGI integration. Laika created an action-adventure with emotional depth rivaling any Pixar film.
details.whyItMatters: Kubo proved stop-motion could deliver epic spectacle, not just intimate stories. Its technical ambition showed the medium has no ceiling on scale or narrative scope.
takeaways: Kubo featured the largest stop-motion puppet ever built at 16 feet
CGI was seamlessly integrated to extend practical effects
The film demonstrated stop-motion could handle epic-scale storytelling

faq.question: How was the giant skeleton puppet built and animated?
faq.answer: The 16-foot skeleton was too large for traditional frame-by-frame manipulation. Laika built it from modular sections and used a combination of physical animation and CGI to achieve its massive, fluid movements.

faq.question: How does Kubo blend stop-motion and CGI?
faq.answer: Physical puppets and sets were animated traditionally, then CGI extended environments, added effects like water and fire, and enhanced puppet movements. The blend is so seamless that most viewers cannot distinguish the techniques.
